verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding quotes its own refutation. Its evidence that MIND signed no orders in the May-July quarter is a set of dated posts in docs/99c2756f5a8cd4ac8707f17d2da857799770ed0a.txt, and those posts are the corpus record that the fact was known and being acted on: 'there has been a prolonged absence of new order announcements' (2026-08-25T18:50:10Z), 'I cant even remember when there were latest orders?!' (2026-08-20T15:49:27Z), 'Still radio silence, what's the plan?' (2026-07-28T23:51:01Z), 'RFP awards need to be announced immediately' (2026-08-25). This is not an obscure filing-index inference that reached nobody - it is the dominant complaint of the holder base for six straight weeks, alongside 'the market has no confidence in your plan or execution' (08-28) and a proxy-vote protest. Then the tape: baselines/MIND.json has pct_from_52w_low at exactly 0.0, pct_from_52w_high at -70.61% and run_up_20d_pct at -16.33%, and the digest itself records '52 week low posted today' on 2026-08-20. A stock making new 52-week lows through the precise window in which the orders did not arrive is the market pricing the drought in real time; the finding cannot both cite the drawdown as context and claim the cause is unpriced. Its one piece of contrary evidence is a single retail poster 'just kinda feeling it' about a $10.2m order - a hope, not a price. The finding's own second support closes the loop: short interest falling from 968,000 to 415,000 means the de-rating was long liquidation, i.e. holders selling on the absence of orders rather than shorts pressing.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 'We already know there is some softness to the business and there has been a prolonged absence of new order announcements' - the finding's central fact, published two weeks before the print, prefaced with 'we already know'.
'52 week low posted today' and 'I cant even remember when there were latest orders?!' on the same date - the drought and the price mark together.
The only 8-K between the April results and the print is item 5.07, annual meeting results - the absence of order 8-Ks is verifiable from the public index at any time.

TGS's CEO attributing lower oil prices to Middle East de-escalation and framing exploration growth as 'over the coming years' - the sector read the finding concedes is not supportive was itself published.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json and the sealed baseline (amc, so the 09-08 close of 4.20 is pre-print and admissible): spot 4.20 with pct_from_52w_low 0.0 - the stock is AT its 52-week low on the day it reports - run_up_20d_pct -16.33%, run_up_5d_pct -3.45%, 70.61% below the 52-week high, on a 108,535-share average. Six of the last seven prints produced negative reactions (-5.40, -28.47, -24.06, -14.54, -10.81 against +26.47 and +42.32 in 2025-04 and 2024-12), so a poor print at this name is the base case in the anchor everyone holds. The 12.03% deadband on a median 24.06% reaction means the bar for this claim to be 'new' is very high.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated statement of the size of the pending bid pipeline or of backlog as of 31 July that is materially different from the $13.9m the Q1 call disclosed - a number, rather than the absence of announcements, which the holder base has already discounted.

interactions: The finding states that both of its supports and its main quotes come from the same digest and should be collapsed into one source cluster; that same digest is also my primary evidence of prior publication, so the corroboration and the refutation are the identical document. Only the filings-index absence is independent, and that is an absence rather than a disclosure.
corpus_limits: No analyst note, consensus estimate or preview exists for MIND anywhere in the capture, so I cannot test whether the sell side had modelled orders that did not arrive; that absence is a capture artefact of the queries run, not evidence about the world. No 8-K or 10-Q bodies are stored, so the $13.9m backlog and the 'by multiples' pipeline comment are only available at digest precision and I could not read the Q1 filing itself. No option chain. No tripwire-flagged documents excluded.
